59	### Algorithm
60	
61	This procedure reads files under the plugin root. The main agent resolves the plugin root from its shell variable `$TOOLBOX_PLUGIN_ROOT`; a Read-only sub-agent uses the absolute plugin-root path injected into its prompt under `## Plugin Root` (see its agent definition). Substitute that resolved path for the plugin-root prefix in every `…/profiles/…` read below.
62	
63	1. **Iterate profiles.** For each §Known profiles `<name>`:
64	   1. Use the `Read` tool on `${TOOLBOX_PLUGIN_ROOT}/profiles/<name>/DETECTION.md`.
65	   2. If `Read` fails with ENOENT (profile name in list but directory missing — a stale list entry), skip silently and move on.
66	   3. If `Read` succeeds, parse the declared `## Path signals`, `## Filename signals`, and `## Content signals` sections.
67	
68	2. **Evaluate in cost order.** For each input file, check signals in this order: path → filename → content. Cheapest first.
69	3. **Apply the authority rule.** A file activates the profile only if a **filename signal** OR **content signal** matches.
70	   A path-only match does NOT activate. Paths are a pre-filter that promotes files to "candidates"; authoritative activation requires filename or content confirmation.
71	   A file that matches NO path signal is still evaluated against filename and content signals — path pre-filtering is a cost hint, not a gate.
72	   (Otherwise a `Chart.yaml` at a non-standard path would be missed.)
73	4. **Bound content inspection.** Read at most ~16 KB per file when evaluating content signals.
74	   Multi-document YAML is inspected per `---`-separated block — a file may have five blocks, and only the third need match for the file to activate the profile.
75	5. **Collect records.** Accumulate one record per matched profile with the triggering files and the signal descriptions that fired.
76	
77	### Tool choice
78	
79	A consumer may consolidate instruction reads into bounded packets containing
80	the complete, unmodified source bodies, original paths and hashes. Read every
81	packet part completely before applying those instructions; the original paths
82	still determine link resolution and detection provenance. A manifest, checksum,
83	requested read or truncated packet alone does not establish loading. This
84	changes packaging only: evaluate every Known-profile rule and each index
85	conditional exactly as below. Direct file reads remain the default fallback.
86	
87	- Single file at `${TOOLBOX_PLUGIN_ROOT}/…` → `Read`. This is what the algorithm uses.
88	- Enumeration across profiles → iterate the §Known profiles list, `Read` each. Never `Glob` (cwd-scoped, misses outside-cwd paths).
89	
90	### Two dimensions: cost vs authority
91	
92	Signals live on two axes that point in different directions. Keep them separate in your mental model:
93	
94	- **Evaluation cost** (cheapest first): path < filename < content.
95	  Path globs touch only the path string;
96	  filename matches are exact string compares;
97	  content inspection opens the file.
98	- **Authority** (most authoritative first): filename ≈ content > path.
99	  A filename or content match activates the profile; a path-only match does not.
100	  Filename and content are equally authoritative, but filename resolves first at runtime — a filename match short-circuits content inspection for that file.
101	
102	Evaluating cheapest-first optimizes work. Applying authority correctly prevents false positives from incidental path matches — a stray `manifests/` directory in a Go project does not make the project Kubernetes.
103	
104	### Plugin-root resolution failure
105	
106	If every `Read` attempt in Algorithm step 1 fails — i.e., the plugin root could not be resolved (the variable is unset for the main agent, or no `## Plugin Root` path was provided to a sub-agent) or the paths do not exist — the procedure cannot continue.
107	
108	On that failure:
109	
110	1. Emit an actionable error pointing to `CLAUDE.md` §Profile Conventions.
111	2. Return an empty result set so the calling skill falls back to generic guidance rather than panicking.
112	3. Do not retry; do not silently guess a path.
113	
114	Consumers inherit this check by invoking the shared procedure — no skill re-implements it.
115	
116	### Output shape
117	
118	A list of records, one per matched profile:
119	
120	```
121	[
122	  {
123	    profile: "<name>",                     // directory name under profiles/
124	    triggered_by: [
125	      "filename: Chart.yaml",              // signal type + matched value
126	      "content: apiVersion+kind in block 2"
127	    ],
128	    files: [
129	      "path/to/file1.yaml",
130	      "path/to/file2.yaml"
131	    ]
132	  },
133	  ...
134	]
135	```
136	
137	Field semantics:
138	
139	- `profile` — the directory name under `profiles/` (e.g., `go`, `python`, `k8s`).
140	  Used downstream to resolve `profiles/<profile>/<phase>/index.md`,
141	  where `<phase>` is the profile phase subdirectory named identically to the calling skill:
142	  `review-code/`, `review-spec/`, `design/`, `implement/`, `test/`, or `document/`.
143	- `triggered_by` — which signal type fired and the specific value that matched.
144	  For debugging and for explaining detection to the user; never used as the key for profile lookup.
145	- `files` — the subset of input files that activated this profile.
146	  Skills use this to scope behavior (e.g., `helm lint` runs only on files triggered under Helm filename signals, not on every YAML in the diff).
147	
148	When no profile matches, return the empty list `[]`. The caller falls back to generic guidance, identical to today's "no language detected" path.
149
